findings.claim: The summary and evaluator communicate nested reference sharing but omit two stronger limits on fresh-result expectations and do not explicitly identify the README's always-new-object overstatement.
evidence: @investigram-15cfc298 says the README account is broadly borne out subject to its reference-sharing caveat.
@investigram-f207fe80 says nested values can retain source references when recursive overlap does not rebuild them; evaluator answers 2 and 4 retain that caveat and propose further aliasing inquiry.
Frozen reference states that non-plain inputs can be returned directly, zero extra inputs return the original, and the README's always-new-object wording is broader than the source supports.
findings.consequence: A reader learns that nested values can alias inputs but may still expect a newly allocated top-level result in cases where the reference says the original input is returned. The proposed next inquiry is sensible but does not supply the omitted information.
findings.uncertainty: Neither the summary nor evaluator explicitly promises a fresh result for every call. This is an omission and residual ambiguity, not an established false generation claim or evaluator extrapolation.

findings.claim: The descriptor qualification does not explicitly communicate that reading properties can evaluate getters.
evidence: @investigram-f207fe80 says accessors and other descriptor attributes are not preserved and that value properties are materialized.
Evaluator answer 2 repeats non-preservation of accessors and descriptor attributes.
Frozen reference for merge.ts lines 19–36 explicitly states that the implementation does not avoid evaluating getters.
findings.consequence: The view explains the shape of copied properties but leaves a consequential source-reading side effect unstated.
findings.uncertainty: Neither the view nor evaluator claims getter-free behavior. The omission's practical importance depends on whether inputs contain getters.

subjectUsefulness.judgment: Useful for qualified initial understanding of this delegated merge API and for identifying a focused follow-up about reference sharing; insufficient to validate correction handling, runtime behavior or every detailed type claim.
reasons: The summary follows entry-point delegation and communicates runtime merging, array policy and compile-time typing as distinct responsibilities consistent with the frozen reference's principal conclusions.
The evaluator preserves source-versus-execution qualifications and accurately interprets empty revision records, composition and subject provenance.
The proposed inquiry into aliasing is relevant, while missing direct-return and zero-extra-input cases leave the fresh-result limits incompletely communicated.
Visible repetition and identifier density provide concrete presentation feedback, but no actual evaluator misunderstanding is demonstrated.
No generation error repeated by the evaluator or unsupported evaluator extrapolation is established by these supplied artifacts.
limitations: Assessment uses only the supplied frozen reference, captured views, evaluator response and rubric; no repository source or external materials were inspected and no subject execution was performed.

Only summary outputs are supplied. No actual correction, conflict, replacement inspection or reconsideration chain is available to assess milestone-5 behavior beyond the displayed policy and empty statuses.
The frozen reference does not settle detailed type internals, external is-what behavior, full runtime outcomes or interactive usability.

The reference identifies TypeScript 6.0.3 with the approved override setting ignoreDeprecations to 6.0 over the inherited @cycraft/tsconfig 0.1.2 configuration. This assessment makes no new run or equivalence claim and does not attribute observations to the unmodified configuration.
